sources.title: Somaliland Constitution: Somali text and parallel English translation
sources.note: Indexed original heading read; direct fetch fails. English parallel at https://www.somalilandlaw.com/somaliland_constitution.htm, translated by Ibrahim Hashi Jama, April 2000 with April 2005 annotations, also read through original index. The two pages are one constitutional work for budget purposes. The same exact two-word sample is independently visible in the indexed government-hosted constitutional packet at https://som.slmof.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/06/Dastuurka-Jamhuuriyadda-Somaliland-1.pdf, printed page 4 (Supreme Court covering letter of 14 June 2001). Referendum 31 May 2001; Articles 1, 38 and 57. The title is a constitutional claim, not independent international recognition.

sources.title: European External Action Service: Israel/Somalia statement, 27 December 2025
sources.note: Direct official statement read: Israel recognition on 26 December, EU support for Somalia’s unity and territorial integrity, dialogue encouraged. Claims are explicitly dated; no exhaustive current recognition list asserted.

sources.title: UK Parliament: written answer HL2690, 27 November 2024
sources.note: Direct parliamentary answer read. Election 13 November; preliminary international observer assessment, not a final independent certification by this card.

sources.title: Edna Adan University Hospital: history and mission
sources.note: Direct institutional history read. Construction on former garbage dump in 1998, operational 9 March 2002. Training 1,000 midwives is a stated goal, not a claimed completed total. Undated website achievement counters not reused.

sources.title: UNICEF: School enrollment in Somaliland, 30 November 2022
sources.note: Direct original story read. Qoryaley Primary School, Rahma Abdirashid aged 12, afternoon shifts and sorghum porridge with dates and milk. Dated local example rather than universal education custom.

sources.title: UNICEF Somalia Annual Report 2015: Opening a tap that helps keep children in school
sources.note: Full PDF text read, printed pp. 16 to 17, human PDF pp. 22 to 23. Dhabolaq Primary School, Hamsa, solar pump, capped well and storage tank. The paragraph on toilet cleaning is Hamsa’s account.

sources.title: UNICEF: Sustained water supply for children and women in Somaliland, 2 December 2018
sources.note: Direct original release read. Four named town networks and Tog Wajaale’s prior reliance on earth-dam water. Infrastructure report, not a claim that water shortages ended.

sources.title: Hargeysa Cultural Centre: The Library
sources.note: Direct centre description read. Established 2014; ground-floor general library, children’s games, upstairs research collections, browsing without membership and membership for borrowing.

sources.title: DP World: new terminal at Berbera Port, 24 June 2021
sources.note: Direct operator announcement read. Completed first phase has 400-metre quay and three ship-to-shore gantry cranes. Announced future expansion and projected trade effects not treated as completed outcomes.

sources.title: French Senate: Djibouti, Eritrea and Ethiopia, 2004 report
sources.note: Direct original report read, section I.1. Used for 1896, 1967, 1977 chronology; modern demographic numbers and promotional account of French influence not reused.

sources.title: US Air Force Culture and Language Center: Djibouti field guide, historical chapter
sources.note: Full PDF downloaded and locally extracted as djibouti-guide.txt. Human PDF page 27, World War II: Vichy, blockade, Nouailhetas’s repression, famine and late 1942 transition. Simplified statement that no supplies could enter is not adopted; British contemporary account separately documents dhow traffic.

sources.title: British Museum: Issa wooden milk vessel, Af1934,0717.25
sources.note: Direct full museum catalogue read. Made circa 1930 to 1934, acquired at Rahale, donated by colonial officer Alexander Tancred Curle in 1934. Description, dimensions and collector’s recorded purpose distinguished from present-day usage.

sources.title: French Somali Coast: Arrêté 753 on prices, 29 July 1938
sources.note: Full indexed original eJO transcription read, edition 500 of 31 July 1938. Preamble and Articles 2 to 3. Regulations describe prescribed controls, not proof that every listed good was locally stocked or affordable. Obvious OCR damage outside quoted phrase not reproduced.

sources.title: French Somali Coast: Arrêté 41 on school inspection, 16 January 1941
sources.note: Full indexed original transcription read earlier in this research sequence; direct fetch unavailable. Edition 530 of 31 January 1941; preamble and Article 1 distinguish public, private and rural school inspection. OCR errors in unrelated reference dates not reused.

sources.title: French Somali Coast: Arrêté 105 reorganizing the colonial militia, 3 February 1943
sources.note: Direct full official transcription read, edition 4 of 15 February 1943. Articles 56, 60 to 61 and 76 to 78. Public passages explicitly concern requirements/entitlements, not proof of actual delivery to every soldier.

sources.title: British Military Administration of Occupied Territories in Africa, 1941 to 1947: Assab and the Djibouti blockade
sources.note: Full indexed original passage read; web direct PDF fetch rejected for 13.9 MB size. Assab section: Aussa liaison, livestock purchases, cloth offered, blockade lifted 24 March 1942 because dhow traffic could not be stopped. Claims attributed to the British account; its dismissive descriptions of African authorities not adopted.

sources.title: Richard A. Lester, International Aspects of Wartime Monetary Experience (1944)
sources.note: Indexed original printed p. 7 read in full. Princeton Essays in International Finance no. 3, August 1944. Djibuti franc exchange in January 1943 and progressive levy; footnote 10 gives thresholds. Author presents anti-inflation purpose as apparent, so no definitive policy motive claimed.
